Description: Five years after the Great Fire of 1845 burned a third of Pittsburgh, the rebuilt brick city of 46,000 smokes with glassworks, rolling mills, foundries and boatyards. Choose your industry and where to found your works.
Suggested Action: Choice: game start. Pick an industry and a site and found the works; the 1850 town is seeded around the Point.

Description: Irish refugees from the Great Famine and Germans fleeing the failed revolutions of 1848 arrive by canal and river, settling in the Point, Lawrenceville and Allegheny City.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Irish and German migrants settle the Point, Lawrenceville and Allegheny City; first Catholic and Lutheran churches appear there.

Description: Congress passes the Fugitive Slave Act. Pittsburgh's Black community meets in protest, Martin Delany vows resistance, and hundreds flee to Canada within weeks.
Suggested Action: Effect: small Black population drop in the Hill and Arthursville for a few seasons. Choice: let your works shelter fugitives (reputation up, risk of federal fine).

Description: McKeesport, a coal-mining village since 1830, gets its first iron and steel mill.
Suggested Action: Spawn: small iron mill founded at McKeesport (neutral owner); McKeesport becomes a valid site with a starter labor pool.

Description: The first railroad reaches Allegheny City from the west, beginning the end of the canal era.
Suggested Action: Spawn: open the Fort Wayne line into Allegheny City; rail shipping available to works within reach of it.

Description: Bernard Lauth and B.F. Jones found the American Iron Company on the Monongahela south of the city: the seed of Jones & Laughlin.
Suggested Action: Rival: Jones & Laughlin founds the American Iron Works on the South Side (already scheduled for 1853; move entry to 1852).

Description: The Pennsylvania Railroad opens its line over the mountains. Philadelphia is now hours, not days, away; the canal and the Conestoga wagon fade.
Suggested Action: Spawn: open the PRR main line; east-bound rail shipping cost drops; canal shipping cost rises.

Description: The city's first chartered public hospital opens a four-story, 120-patient building in the 12th Ward.
Suggested Action: Spawn: hospital in Polish Hill/Bloomfield edge; lowers epidemic losses in nearby wards.

Description: Cholera sweeps the crowded riverfront wards. Hundreds die; families flee to the hills.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): epidemic in crowded tiles. Choice: fund a pest house/clean water for your workers' ward to halve losses there.

Description: Banker James Laughlin buys out Lauth's share of the American Iron Company. Its American Mine opens to feed the furnaces with coal.
Suggested Action: Rival: J&L gains capital (faster expansion); opens a drift mine above the South Side works.

Description: Twice burned out, Western University finishes a 16-room brick building at Ross and Diamond Streets. Classes resume the next year.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Western University building downtown at Ross and Diamond.

Description: Pittsburgh opens Central High School, one of the region's first public high schools.
Suggested Action: Spawn: high school downtown; slightly raises skilled-labor share in the city wards.

Description: Anti-slavery delegates meet in Pittsburgh, form the first Republican National Committee, and call the convention that will nominate Frémont.
Suggested Action: Choice: back the new Republican party (protective tariff later, Free Soil reputation) or the Democrats (cheap immigrant labor support).

Description: Pennsylvania sells its canal and portage railroad to the Pennsylvania Railroad for $7.5 million. Within a year the Philadelphia route is all-rail.
Suggested Action: Effect: canal shipping retires; all eastbound freight goes by the PRR at higher rail rates for 4 seasons.

Description: A financial panic spreads from New York. Iron prices collapse and mills bank their furnaces.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): price drop. Choice: bank furnaces (cut wages bill, lose skilled men) or run at a loss.

Description: Iron puddlers found the Sons of Vulcan at a Diamond Street hotel bar, with Miles Humphreys as Grand Master. It becomes one of the era's strongest unions.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): wages up. Unlock: union lodges appear in iron towns; Choice: recognize the puddlers' union or blacklist members.

Description: Edwin Drake strikes oil up the Allegheny. Refineries spring up along Pittsburgh's riverbanks and barges of crude crowd the wharves.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Spawn: oil refineries and barge traffic along the Allegheny shore; Glass and Metalworking demand up a little (lamps, barrels, tanks).

Description: President-elect Lincoln speaks at the Monongahela House on his way to Washington.
Suggested Action: Spawn: crowd at the Monongahela House; morale up for a season.

Description: The Secretary of War orders heavy guns shipped from the Allegheny Arsenal to Southern forts. A mass meeting blocks the shipment, and the order is countermanded.
Suggested Action: Choice: join the mass meeting (Union reputation up, early war contracts) or stay out.

Description: The Union calls for men and guns. The Fort Pitt Foundry casts great Rodman cannon; every mill runs night and day.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): price up. Choice: bid for Union contracts (cannon, plate, rail) for guaranteed sales; men enlist and labor pool shrinks.

Description: The first firm bearing the Jones and Laughlin name is organized, headquartered at Third and Ross downtown.
Suggested Action: Rival: rename the South Side rival to Jones & Laughlin; it adds a second furnace.

Event Name: Dixmont Asylum; West Penn Goes to War
Description: Western Pennsylvania's first mental hospital opens at Dixmont. The Army takes over West Penn Hospital as a military hospital for three years.
Suggested Action: Spawn: West Penn marked as a military hospital (no civilian care) until 1865.

Description: An explosion tears through the Allegheny Arsenal's cartridge laboratory in Lawrenceville, killing 78 workers, most of them young women.
Suggested Action: Spawn: ruin at the Arsenal in Lawrenceville; small population loss there. Choice: fund a safety inspector (cost) to cut future accident risk.

Event Name: Defences Thrown Up on the Hills
Description: As Lee's army invades Pennsylvania, thousands of workers dig earthworks on the hills around the city. The rebels turn back at Gettysburg.
Suggested Action: Spawn: earthwork forts on Coal Hill and Herron Hill. Effect: works lose half their labor for one season while men dig.

Event Name: Iron Wages Tied to Iron Prices
Description: Ending an eight-month strike, ironmasters sign the Vulcans' first contract: a sliding scale linking puddlers' pay to the price of bar iron.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): wages up. Unlock: sliding-scale wage policy (wages follow price) as a labor option.

Description: Peace returns. War contracts end, but railroads and cities across the country need iron as never before.
Suggested Action: Effect: war contracts end; demand shifts to rail. Choice: retool for rails (cost, better prices to 1873).

Description: The state lets railroads commission private police. A year later the power extends to coal and iron companies, at $1 per commission.
Suggested Action: Unlock: hire company police (cost per season): lower strike chance, higher unrest and death risk in strikes.

Description: The Allegheny Observatory passes to Western University. Samuel Langley becomes director two years later.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Allegheny Observatory on the Allegheny hills; small reputation if you donate.

Description: Allegheny City turns its old common pasture into a landscaped public park.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Allegheny Commons park (already drawn) opens; nearby land value up.

Description: Failed strikes break 11 Sons of Vulcan locals this year and 16 more the next.
Suggested Action: Effect: union lodges close in a few towns; wages slip back.

Description: A visiting writer describes the smoky valley at night as 'hell with the lid off'. The name sticks.
Suggested Action: Effect: none. Show the valley at night (zoomed out, furnace glow) behind the headline; works with high pollution get a reputation dent.

Event Name: The City Annexes the East End
Description: Pittsburgh annexes Lawrenceville, Oakland, East Liberty and the farms beyond, tripling its area.
Suggested Action: Spawn: city boundary moves east; East End gets city water and police; taxes apply to works there.

Description: Young George Westinghouse receives his patent for a railroad air brake.
Suggested Action: Unlock: rail-safety demand; Metalworking players can bid to license air-brake work.

Description: Henry J. Heinz and L.C. Noble form Heinz, Noble & Company in Sharpsburg to sell bottled horseradish.
Suggested Action: Off-map (Sharpsburg). Effect: Glass bottle demand up for 8 seasons.

Description: The Westinghouse Air Brake Company is incorporated and starts production in Pittsburgh the next year.
Suggested Action: Rival: Westinghouse Air Brake plant opens on the North Side (Metalworking rival).

Description: A college for women, the future Chatham, is founded in Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Spawn: women's college in Shadyside.

Description: The first passenger incline lifts workers up Coal Hill to the new streets of Mt. Washington.
Suggested Action: Spawn (existing): incline opens; Mt. Washington fills in.

Description: The Fifteenth Amendment is ratified. Black Pennsylvanians, disfranchised since 1838, can vote again.
Suggested Action: Effect: Black voters count in ward politics; Hill District political weight up.

Description: Westinghouse Air Brake becomes one of the first American firms to give workers a Saturday half-day.
Suggested Action: Unlock: Saturday half-holiday labor policy (small output cost, lower strike chance, better hiring).

Description: Henry Clay Frick, 21, joins two cousins and a friend to turn Connellsville coal into coke.
Suggested Action: Off-map: Connellsville coke supply begins; coke price falls for steel and iron.

Event Name: The South Side Joins the City
Description: Birmingham and the other South Side boroughs are annexed to Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Spawn: city boundary takes in Birmingham; city taxes and police apply there.

Description: Carnegie breaks ground for a Bessemer steel works at Braddock's Field, named for the Pennsylvania Railroad's president.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carnegie begins Edgar Thomson at Braddock (construction site sprite until 1875).

Description: The Flagler brothers of Boston open a pipe works at McKeesport. It becomes the fastest-growing town in the nation.
Suggested Action: Rival: National Tube founds a pipe works at McKeesport; McKeesport grows fast.

Description: The collapse of Jay Cooke's bank starts the Long Depression. Orders vanish; wages are cut across the valley.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): prices and wages down. Choice: cut wages 10% (strike risk) or hold wages (cash loss, loyalty up).

Description: Andrew Carnegie's Edgar Thomson Works at Braddock rolls its first Bessemer steel rail. A new age of steel begins.
Suggested Action: Rival: Edgar Thomson starts production; Bessemer tech unlocks for the player's steel works.

Description: The Long Depression sinks young H.J. Heinz's business. He restarts as F & J Heinz and adds ketchup.
Suggested Action: Effect: none. Tip: warn the player if cash would go negative in a depression; bankruptcy ends the company.

Description: At Emerald Hall, Pittsburgh, the Vulcans, Heaters and Roll Hands merge into the Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): wages and strike chance up. Unlock: Amalgamated lodges at iron and steel works; Choice: sign the union scale or not.

Description: Samuel Diescher's incline begins hauling riders up Mount Washington at a grade of up to 30 degrees.
Suggested Action: Spawn (existing): Duquesne Incline opens on Mt. Washington.

Description: Railroad workers strike against wage cuts. Militia fire on a crowd at 28th Street; the crowd burns the Pennsylvania Railroad's roundhouse and hundreds of cars.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): strike. Spawn: burned roundhouse and cars at 28th Street. Choice: ship by river to avoid the shutdown (cost).

Description: Catholic Holy Ghost Fathers found the college that becomes Duquesne University.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Catholic college on the Bluff (future Duquesne University).

Description: Last rails are laid to Youngstown. The P&LE is the only major line free of the Pennsylvania Railroad and is an immediate success.
Suggested Action: Spawn: P&LE line opens along the Mon's south bank; cheaper rail rates for works near it (competition with PRR).

Description: Slovak, Hungarian, Polish and Rusyn labourers begin arriving for mill jobs, recruited by agents and letters home.
Suggested Action: Effect: Slovak, Hungarian, Polish and Rusyn migrants arrive; onion-dome churches appear near steel works.

Description: With loans from the Mellon bank, Frick buys out his partners and forms H.C. Frick & Company.
Suggested Action: Unlock: Mellon bank loans (borrow capital at interest).

Description: The Allegheny County Light Company is founded with $90,000 to sell electric light.
Suggested Action: Unlock: Power industry can sell electric light downtown.

Description: Republican Christopher Magee runs the votes while contractor William Flinn takes the paving and sewer contracts. Their machine will rule the city for two decades.
Suggested Action: Choice: pay the ring for contracts and permits (cheaper roads and land) or refuse (slower permits).

Description: The Pittsburgh Bessemer Steel Company opens a works on the Homestead flats. Carnegie buys it two years later.
Suggested Action: Rival: Homestead Works opens (existing rival entry year).

Description: Westinghouse Air Brake moves to a bigger plant in Allegheny City. Within ten years it builds a company town at Wilmerding.
Suggested Action: Rival: Air Brake plant expands on the North Side.

Description: Westinghouse founds Union Switch & Signal at Swissvale to build railroad signals.
Suggested Action: Rival: Union Switch & Signal plant at Swissvale.

Description: The Coke King meets Andrew Carnegie in New York. Their partnership forms the next year, joining coke to steel.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carnegie and Frick ally; Carnegie's coke cost falls. Choice for steel players: sign a long coke contract with Frick (cheaper, but he gets a say in labor policy).

Description: After the courthouse burns, Western University sells its downtown buildings to Allegheny County and moves out.
Suggested Action: Spawn: courthouse ruin downtown; university leaves.

Description: Father Mollinger completes St. Anthony's Chapel on Troy Hill, with thousands of relics. Pilgrims arrive by the trainload.
Suggested Action: Spawn: St. Anthony's Chapel on Troy Hill; pilgrims visit.

Description: Gustav Lindenthal's lenticular truss bridge replaces Roebling's suspension span over the Monongahela.
Suggested Action: Spawn (existing): bridge changes to the lenticular truss.

Description: John B. Ford and John Pitcairn found Pittsburgh Plate Glass, with its first works at Creighton on the Allegheny.
Suggested Action: Off-map: Creighton. Rival: PPG enters the glass market; Glass players face price competition.

Description: Anarchists meet in Pittsburgh, found the International Working People's Association, and reject reform through the ballot.
Suggested Action: Effect: radical unrest up; strike chance slightly higher for two years.

Description: The rivers rise high in February, flooding wharves and riverfront mills.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): flood hits floodplain works.

Description: Natural gas is piped into Pittsburgh's mills and homes. For a few years the smoke thins and the sky turns blue.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): pollution down. Unlock: switch furnaces to gas (cost, less smoke).

Description: Blast furnaces rise at Rankin across the river from Homestead.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carrie Furnaces at Rankin (blast furnaces sprite).

Description: Shadyside Hospital opens a school of nursing.
Suggested Action: Spawn: nursing school at Shadyside Hospital.

Description: The first dam on the Ohio River opens at Avalon. The great wicket dam gives the harbor deep water in all seasons.
Suggested Action: Effect: deeper water; barge shipping cheaper and possible in low-water seasons.

Description: George Westinghouse founds his electric company to sell alternating current. The battle of the currents begins.
Suggested Action: Rival: Westinghouse Electric enters (existing rival).

Description: Open-hearth furnaces are installed at the Homestead Works.
Suggested Action: Unlock: open-hearth steel tech; rival Homestead upgrades.

Description: After three decades of iron, J&L begins making steel.
Suggested Action: Rival: J&L converts from iron to steel.

Description: A general hospital opens in Allegheny City.
Suggested Action: Spawn: hospital in Allegheny City.

Description: A new charter centralizes city government in departments such as Public Works and Public Safety, which the ring uses to steer contracts.
Suggested Action: Effect: city contracts route through Public Works; ring bribes cost more but get faster results.

Description: Alfred Hunt and Charles Martin Hall open an experimental aluminum smelter on Smallman Street.
Suggested Action: Rival: small aluminum works on Smallman Street (Metalworking).

Description: H. H. Richardson's massive stone courthouse and jail open on Grant's Hill.
Suggested Action: Spawn: new courthouse on Grant's Hill.

Description: On Thanksgiving Day the Smallman Street works pours the first commercial aluminum. The metal sells for nearly $5 a pound.
Suggested Action: Unlock: aluminum as a Metalworking product line.

Description: Heinz gains control of the family firm and renames it the H.J. Heinz Company.
Suggested Action: Effect: Glass bottle and jar demand up for 12 seasons.

Description: The South Fork Dam, owned by a club of Pittsburgh industrialists, fails upriver. More than 2,200 die in Johnstown; relief trains leave from Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Choice: send relief (money; reputation up) or not.

Description: Carnegie personally dedicates the first Carnegie library in America near his Edgar Thomson Works. A basement bathhouse lets millworkers wash before reading.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Carnegie Library in Braddock. Choice: fund a library in your own town (cost; morale up, strike chance down).

Description: Public Works chief Edward Bigelow spends over $900,000 buying farms parcel by parcel for a 377-acre park around the city reservoirs.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Highland Park land bought around the reservoir.

Event Name: Schenley Park Given to the City
Description: Mary Schenley gives 300 acres of land in Oakland for a great public park.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Schenley Park (existing).

Description: The Carnegie Free Library of Allegheny opens. It was the first library Andrew Carnegie commissioned, though Braddock's opened first.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Carnegie Library of Allegheny on the Commons.

Description: The Second Avenue Traction Company runs electric streetcars. Horsecars begin to vanish.
Suggested Action: Spawn (existing): streetcars start; workers can live farther from the works (labor walking radius up).

Description: Congress raises import duties to about 50%, with new protection for tinplate. Pittsburgh steel and glass men cheer, and tinplate mills rise along the Mon.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): price up for steel and glass.

Description: Striking coke workers march on Frick's company store at Morewood. National Guardsmen fire into the crowd of a thousand, killing nine.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): strike chance up. Off-map: coke strike raises coke price for a season.

Description: Pittsburgh Reduction begins smelting at New Kensington, the start of an aluminum town on the Allegheny.
Suggested Action: Off-map: the Smallman Street aluminum works closes; its lot becomes vacant and jobs leave the Strip.

Description: Brothers Frank and Ralph Dravo found a contracting firm in Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Rival: Dravo enters as a contractor (shipbuilding rival later).

Description: Westinghouse installs the nation's first alternating-current power system, at a Colorado mine.
Suggested Action: Unlock: AC transmission for Power (serve customers farther away).

Description: Heinz coins his famous "57 Varieties" slogan.
Suggested Action: Effect: Glass bottle demand up for 8 seasons.

Description: The Western Pennsylvania Medical College merges into Western University.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: Locked-out steelworkers fight Pinkerton guards landing from barges at the Homestead Works. Seven workers and three Pinkertons die; the state militia occupies the town and the union is broken.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): strike. Choice for steel players facing a contract: sign with the Amalgamated, or lock out and hire Pinkertons (strike broken, union gone, reputation down).

Description: Anarchist Alexander Berkman shoots and stabs Henry Clay Frick in his office downtown. Frick survives and returns to work within a week.
Suggested Action: Effect: public sympathy swings to the company; strike support drops (strike chance down for 2 seasons).

Description: On July 1, Carnegie consolidates all his plants into the Carnegie Steel Company, days before the Homestead lockout.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carnegie merges Edgar Thomson, Homestead and Duquesne into one rival (shared cash).

Description: West Penn Hospital opens a nursing school with 15 students.
Suggested Action: Effect: hospital care improves; epidemic losses near West Penn fall slightly.

Description: Nearly bankrupt, the Amalgamated Association votes on November 20 to send its men back to Homestead.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): wages and strike chance down. Spawn: Homestead under militia guard for a season.

Description: Company and union drop their criminal charges against each other, closing the Homestead affair in the courts.
Suggested Action: Effect: militia leaves Homestead; town returns to normal.

Description: Stung by the Homestead barges, Congress bars the federal government from hiring Pinkerton agents or similar private armies.
Suggested Action: Effect: Pinkerton option costs more; company police remain.

Description: Westinghouse alternating current lights the Chicago World's Fair, and the company wins the Niagara Falls generator contract.
Suggested Action: Rival: Westinghouse Electric grows; Power players face tougher competition.

Description: Banks and railroads fail across the country. Mills close; soup kitchens open in the mill towns.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): prices and wages down. Spawn: soup kitchens in mill towns.

Description: Highland Park opens to the public four years after the city began buying land.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Highland Park opens.

Description: An addition gives the Braddock library a 964-seat music hall, gymnasium, swimming pool and bowling alleys. Carnegie employees pay half price.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Braddock library adds music hall, pool and gym.

Description: Henry Phipps gives the city a great glasshouse in Schenley Park and insists it open on Sundays so working people can visit.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Phipps Conservatory in Schenley Park.

Description: The United Mine Workers call a national bituminous coal strike, and pits across the Pittsburgh district go idle.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): output down while coal is short.

Description: Allegheny City's mayor and residents pool money to buy the Watson farm for a 251-acre park crowned by the Allegheny Observatory.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Riverview Park on the North Side hills (observatory site).

Description: Six Croatian benefit societies merge in Allegheny City into a national federation headquartered in Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Croatian hall in Allegheny City.

Description: Banker Andrew Mellon, whose father graduated in 1837, joins Western University's board of trustees.
Suggested Action: Unlock: endow the university (cash for reputation and a later supply of engineers).

Description: Westinghouse generators at Niagara's Adams plant send power about 20 miles to Buffalo.
Suggested Action: Unlock: long-distance AC for the Power player.

Description: Carnegie's library, music hall and museum open in Oakland.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Carnegie Institute in Oakland.

Description: The Pittsburgh Orchestra is founded and plays in Carnegie Music Hall.
Suggested Action: Choice: sponsor the orchestra (cost; reputation with the city elite, cheaper bank loans).

Description: Streetcar magnate Christopher Magee offers the city a zoo, provided it sits in Highland Park at the end of his trolley line.
Suggested Action: Spawn: zoo site marked in Highland Park; trolley line extended to it.

Description: Carnegie's Union Railroad links his works along the Monongahela, moving hot metal and ore between mills.
Suggested Action: Spawn (existing): Union Railroad links the Mon mills.

Description: Westinghouse and General Electric pool their electrical patents, ending the war of the currents in court.
Suggested Action: Effect: Power prices stabilize (smaller price swings).

Description: Frick crushes an attempt to rebuild the union at Homestead. Carnegie also beats union drives at Duquesne and Edgar Thomson.
Suggested Action: Effect: union lodges disappear at Homestead, Duquesne and Edgar Thomson.

Description: Jones & Laughlin refuses to sign with the Amalgamated Association, starting the de-unionization of Pittsburgh's mills.
Suggested Action: Effect: J&L becomes non-union; Choice for the player: follow (wages down, strike risk up) or stay union.

Description: The federal government seizes the private Monongahela Navigation Company's locks and dams by eminent domain. Tolls on coal barges end.
Suggested Action: Effect: Mon River tolls end; barge shipping cheaper on the Mon.

Description: The Carnegie Library's first branch opens, the first in America with open shelves and a children's room.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Lawrenceville branch library.

Description: Ten thousand people, many riding Magee's trolleys, attend the zoo's dedication.
Suggested Action: Spawn: zoo in Highland Park; streetcar traffic there.

Description: George Mesta merges two machine shops into a heavy-machinery maker at West Homestead.
Suggested Action: Rival: Mesta Machine at West Homestead (Metalworking).

Description: Carnegie adds the Rankin blast furnaces across the river to his Homestead empire.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carrie Furnaces pass to Carnegie.

Event Name: Homestead Library Opens Above the Mill
Description: Carnegie's $300,000 library, music hall and athletic club opens on the hill overlooking the works where the 1892 strike was fought.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Carnegie library in Munhall above the Homestead Works.

Description: Sisters Margaret and Stella Stein become Western University's first women graduates.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: Andrew Mellon's Monongahela Street Railway buys the Kenny family's picnic grove to draw riders to the end of the line.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Kenny's Grove marked at West Mifflin; trolley line extended.

Description: The West End branch opens with open stacks.
Suggested Action: Spawn: West End branch library.

Description: State Republican boss Matthew Quay of Beaver is acquitted of misusing state funds. A deadlocked legislature leaves his Senate seat empty for two years.
Suggested Action: Effect: state politics stalled; no new state laws or charters for 2 years.

Description: Three hundred Homestead men secretly form a union lodge. Frick shuts the works down.
Suggested Action: Effect: Homestead rival briefly shuts; local labor pool up.

Description: Mellon's trolley park opens above the Monongahela, drawing three times the zoo's opening crowd.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Kennywood park at West Mifflin; weekend trolley crowds.

Description: Carnegie's fossil hunters find a giant dinosaur skeleton near Medicine Bow. It is named Diplodocus carnegii.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: National Tube merges with 20 pipe makers into the National Tube Company, soon the world's largest steel-pipe producer.
Suggested Action: Rival: McKeesport tube works joins the National Tube trust (more cash).

Description: Dozens of river and rail mines combine into the Pittsburgh Coal Company.
Suggested Action: Effect: coal supply consolidated; coal price up slightly.

Description: Carnegie Steel posts a record net profit of $21 million for the year.
Suggested Action: Effect: show Carnegie's profit in the ledger as a benchmark against the player's.

Description: No unionized steel plant remains in Pennsylvania. Amalgamated membership has fallen from 24,000 to about 8,000 in a decade.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): wages down.

Description: With ten plants, Pittsburgh Plate Glass controls 65% of the nation's plate glass and is its second-largest paint maker.
Suggested Action: Rival: PPG pressure; Glass prices down for players.

Description: J.P. Morgan's interests merge bridge builders into the American Bridge Company, headquartered in Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Rival: American Bridge (Metalworking) gains contracts.

Description: Andrew Carnegie founds a technical school in Oakland to train the sons and daughters of working families.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Carnegie Tech campus starts in Oakland.

Description: Oil gushes at Spindletop, Texas. The Mellons are the largest investors in the venture that becomes Gulf Oil.
Suggested Action: Effect: oil prices fall; fuel cost for gas-fired works down slightly.

Description: J. P. Morgan buys Carnegie Steel for $480 million and forms the United States Steel Corporation, the first billion-dollar company. Dozens of Pittsburgh men become millionaires overnight.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carnegie Steel, National Tube and American Bridge become U.S. Steel. Choice: sell your company to Morgan (game score payout) or stay independent.

Description: Boss Magee dies. The Quay legislature abolishes the elected mayor and lets the governor appoint a "recorder" to run the city.
Suggested Action: Effect: city permits slow down for 2 years.

Description: Philander Knox, Carnegie Steel's lawyer through Homestead and the U.S. Steel merger, becomes Attorney General.
Suggested Action: Effect: antitrust risk for big rivals stays low while Knox is Attorney General (to 1904).

Description: U.S. Steel offers to recognize the union at most sheet mills. AA president Shaffer demands all plants, and Morgan withdraws the offer.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): strike chance up.

Description: Thousands of strikebreakers and no help from the AFL break the strike. The union loses most of its U.S. Steel lodges.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): wages down.

Description: The traction companies combine into Pittsburgh Railways, a 400-mile streetcar monopoly.
Suggested Action: Spawn: streetcar network merged; fares unified.

Description: Phipps gives $30,000 for a teaching hall where schoolchildren take botany classes.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Phipps Botany Hall added.

Description: Lincoln Steffens's magazine exposé lays bare the Magee–Flinn machine to the whole nation.
Suggested Action: Effect: ring bribes become riskier (chance of exposure and fine).

Description: Most of Pittsburgh's electric companies are consolidated into Duquesne Light.
Suggested Action: Rival: Duquesne Light (Power) gets a downtown franchise.

Description: The Pittsburgh Pirates play Boston in the first modern World Series. Boston wins.
Suggested Action: Effect: morale up for a season.

Description: U.S. Steel buys a half-interest in Crucible Steel's furnaces and steel plant at Clairton.
Suggested Action: Rival: U.S. Steel takes a stake at Clairton.

Description: An explosion at Cheswick kills 179 miners and two rescuers. One boy survives. A third of Homestead's Hungarian Reformed congregation is lost.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Effect: miner shortage raises coal price for a season.

Description: Moved by the Harwick rescuers' deaths, Carnegie endows a $5 million fund to honor civilians who risk their lives for others.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: George Gould opens an $800,000 Beaux-Arts terminal and a tunnel through Mount Washington to break the Pennsylvania Railroad's grip.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Wabash terminal downtown and Wabash bridge; third rail option for shippers.

Description: A plaster cast of Carnegie's dinosaur is unveiled in London, the first of many given to the world's museums.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: Jones & Laughlin begins a vast new works and company town at Aliquippa on the Ohio.
Suggested Action: Off-map: J&L capacity grows; steel prices slightly lower.

Description: American Bridge incorporates a company town on the old Harmony Society lands. It will grow from 5,000 to 20,000 people in twenty years.
Suggested Action: Off-map: American Bridge moves big jobs downriver; Metalworking prices slightly lower.

Description: Reformer George Guthrie wins the mayoralty on a fusion ticket against the Republican organization.
Suggested Action: Effect: ring bribes unavailable for 4 years.

Description: Westinghouse sets up a formal research and development department.
Suggested Action: Unlock: research department option for Power players (faster tech).

Description: Pittsburgh Reduction renames itself the Aluminum Company of America. Mellon's brother Richard is president.
Suggested Action: Effect: aluminum price falls; Metalworking aluminum product line cheaper to source.

Description: Mellon oil interests, including Guffey Petroleum, combine into the Gulf Oil Corporation.
Suggested Action: Effect: Mellon bank stronger; loan rates fall slightly.

Description: Dallas conglomerate Ling-Temco-Vought buys 63% of J&L for about $428 million. Control of a Pittsburgh giant moves to Texas.
Suggested Action: Rival: J&L now owned from Dallas; it stops reinvesting in its Pittsburgh works (rival tech frozen). Choice: accept an outside conglomerate's buyout offer (cash now) or stay independent.

Description: The first new regional park opens in Monroeville and Plum, with the county's only ski slope.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Effect: none on map.

Description: American Standard buys Westinghouse Air Brake.
Suggested Action: Rival: Air Brake sold to American Standard; Wilmerding off-map loses local control.

Description: A job-training center opens on the North Side.
Suggested Action: Unlock: North Side job training lowers unemployment there.

Description: Pittsburgh Plate Glass renames itself PPG Industries.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: Mary Flinn Lawrence offers her 629-acre estate and mansion to the county.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Effect: none on map.

Description: Nate Smith's Black Construction Coalition shuts down public building sites, including Three Rivers Stadium, demanding jobs in the all-white trades.
Suggested Action: Effect: public construction (stadium, renewal) halts a season. Choice: open your skilled trades to Black workers (labor pool up, union friction) or not.

Description: Councilman Pete Flaherty beats the Democratic machine's candidate and wins the mayoralty, promising to cut patronage.
Suggested Action: Effect: city patronage cut; city tax and fee favors end; city budget tighter (fewer public works).

Description: The Pirates and Steelers move to a new stadium on the North Side.
Suggested Action: Spawn: stadium on the North Side shore.

Description: West Penn's Mellon Pavilion opens with a burn care unit serving the mill district.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: Roberto Clemente leads the Pirates to a World Series title.
Suggested Action: Effect: morale up for a season.

Description: Heinz money turns the shuttered Loew's Penn into a $10 million home for the Pittsburgh Symphony.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Heinz Hall downtown (old Loew's Penn restored).

Description: The wettest storm in Pennsylvania's history drives 100,000 from their homes. The Allegheny rises seven inches an hour.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): flood.

Description: Steel mills stop dumping slag in the Nine Mile Run valley.
Suggested Action: Effect: slag pours at Nine Mile Run stop; steel works must pay to haul slag (cost up).

Description: U.S. Steel and the county agree to clean Clairton's air within ten years. An EPA official calls the plant "Dante's Inferno."
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): pollution down. Choice for players with coke ovens: sign a cleanup decree (big cost over 10 years) or fight it in court (fines risk).

Description: Franco Harris's last-second catch gives the Steelers their first playoff win.
Suggested Action: Effect: morale up for a season.

Description: The state and county sue U.S. Steel over 241 air-pollution violations at Clairton.
Suggested Action: Effect: pollution fines on any works above a pollution threshold, charged per season.

Description: The steelworkers and ten steelmakers sign the Experimental Negotiating Agreement, trading national strikes for 3% yearly raises, cost-of-living pay and arbitration.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): strikes rare, wages up 3% a year. Choice for steel players: join the deal (labor peace, rising cost) or bargain alone.

Description: The Arab oil embargo sends energy prices soaring. Detroit's car sales, and its steel orders, fall.
Suggested Action: Effect: car-steel demand falls; energy costs up for all works.

Description: The fountain at the Point is turned on, completing the park where Fort Pitt stood.
Suggested Action: Spawn: fountain at the Point.

Description: After 85 years, the Braddock Carnegie Library closes. The declining mill town cannot fix its roof.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Braddock library boarded up; Braddock morale down. Choice: fund the repairs (cost; reputation up).

Description: U.S. Steel announces a $100 million cleanup at Clairton. The state environment secretary calls the plant a national disgrace.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): pollution down.

Description: The Steelers win their first Super Bowl.
Suggested Action: Effect: morale up for a season.

Description: Gulf Oil's chairman and other executives are forced out over illegal political contributions.
Suggested Action: Effect: if the player made political payments, chance of exposure, fines and reputation loss.

Description: A regional air-pollution emergency centers on Clairton. The EPA links it to 14 deaths, and U.S. Steel warns it cannot make steel without the coke.
Suggested Action: Effect: air emergency: coke and steel works must cut output by half for one season, or pay large fines.

Description: Soaring uranium prices break Westinghouse's fixed-price fuel contracts. Lawsuits will cost it $950 million.
Suggested Action: Rival: Westinghouse Electric weakened; Power market share opens for the player.

Description: Volkswagen chooses New Stanton for its American plant with a $40 million state loan. It will employ over 6,000.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Effect: some skilled workers leave for VW jobs; labor pool shrinks a little.

Description: Beaver Valley Unit 1 is commissioned at Shippingport.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Rival: Duquesne Light adds nuclear capacity; Power prices fall.

Description: Hill District legislator K. Leroy Irvis becomes the first Black speaker of any state legislature since Reconstruction.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: Flaherty leaves for the Justice Department. Council president Richard Caliguiri becomes mayor and wins election as an independent.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: One of the nation's first bus-only roads opens to the South Hills.
Suggested Action: Effect: South Hills commute faster; South Hills suburbs keep growing as city wards shrink.

Event Name: J&L Cuts Back in the City
Description: Jones & Laughlin announces closures at its Pittsburgh works, one of the first big shutdowns in the city.
Suggested Action: Rival: J&L closes part of its Pittsburgh works; laid-off workers join the labor pool or leave.

Description: Mayor Caliguiri announces a second downtown building boom of new office towers.
Suggested Action: Spawn: new office towers downtown; downtown jobs shift from mills to offices.

Description: Rankin's great Furnaces 6 and 7 shut down after seventy years; the last smaller furnaces follow in 1982.
Suggested Action: Rival: Carrie Furnaces shut; Rankin loses jobs and population; furnaces stay as a cold ruin.

Description: LTV's Jones & Laughlin absorbs Youngstown Sheet & Tube.
Suggested Action: Rival: J&L's owner spends on Ohio mills, not Pittsburgh.

Description: The accident at Three Mile Island near Harrisburg freezes nuclear construction and sends utility stocks down.
Suggested Action: Effect: nuclear works' costs +20% for five years; power price +5% (lost capacity); Duquesne Light and the power stocks fall.

Description: Iran's revolution doubles the price of oil; coal prices follow and the valley's power plants pay for it.
Suggested Action: Effect: raw materials +12% for two years, power works +20%; steel orders fall.

Description: The Pirates win the World Series and the Steelers will win a fourth Super Bowl in January.
Suggested Action: Effect: morale up for a season; layoffs feel lighter for one turn.

Description: U.S. Steel announces the shutdown of plants across the country. Imports, old open hearths and lost markets catch up with the valley.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): price down. Choice: close your oldest open hearths now (layoffs, lower costs) or keep them running (losses grow).

Description: The census counts 423,938 people, down more than a third from the 1950 peak.
Suggested Action: Effect: none. Show the population graph since 1950.

Description: Steel demand collapses in a deep recession. Layoffs spread through every mill town.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): price and output down. Choice: lay off workers (unrest, abandonment in town) or carry them at a loss.

Description: U.S. Steel shuts major operations at McKeesport's tube works, laying off 2,400 of 4,800.
Suggested Action: Rival: McKeesport tube works lays off half its workers; McKeesport shops start closing.

Description: Dravo closes its Neville Island shipyard.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Rival: Dravo's shipyard closes; Shipbuilding market opens or collapses (player's choice to bid).

Description: Westinghouse acquires robot maker Unimation.
Suggested Action: Unlock: automation (fewer workers, lower unit cost; layoffs raise unrest).

Description: Carnegie Mellon begins building a campus-wide computer network. Its research budget has grown nearly tenfold.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Hint at a post-steel economy.

Description: Nearly one in five workers in the Monongahela Valley is out of work. Food banks open in union halls.
Suggested Action: Effect: unemployment peaks; vacant houses spread; food banks appear in union halls. Choice: keep workers on at a loss or lay off.

Description: Mesta Machine files for bankruptcy. Most of the West Homestead works is sold by summer.
Suggested Action: Rival: Mesta closes; West Homestead works empties.

Description: The 6.8-mile Martin Luther King Jr. East Busway opens to Wilkinsburg.
Suggested Action: Effect: East End commute faster.

Description: American Bridge ends operations in the town it built.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Rival: American Bridge leaves; Metalworking market shrinks.

Description: Residents buy the doomed Braddock library for $1 and reopen a children's library.
Suggested Action: Spawn: Braddock library reopens (children's library).

Description: Employees buy the Weirton steel works, creating the nation's largest employee-owned manufacturer, in exchange for a six-year wage freeze.
Suggested Action: Unlock: employee buyout: player may sell the works to its workers (wage freeze, plant stays open).

Description: U.S. Steel shuts the Duquesne Works. A campaign to save its giant 'Dorothy Six' blast furnace fails.
Suggested Action: Rival: Duquesne Works closes; Dorothy Six goes cold. Choice: try to buy Dorothy Six with the union and town (cost, risky) or let it go.

Description: Fending off raider T. Boone Pickens, Gulf accepts Chevron's $13.2 billion offer, the largest merger in history.
Suggested Action: Effect: Gulf headquarters leaves; downtown office jobs fall in 1985.

Description: Washington approves the merger of J&L and Republic. The new LTV Steel ranks second in the nation, and the J&L name disappears.
Suggested Action: Rival: J&L renamed LTV Steel; its Pittsburgh works drawn as LTV.

Description: Modern light-rail cars begin running from South Hills Village through a new Mount Lebanon tunnel.
Suggested Action: Spawn: light rail replaces streetcars to the South Hills.

Description: Radical clergy and jobless steelworkers disrupt a church Christmas party with skunk-oil balloons to shame U.S. Steel's chairman.
Suggested Action: Effect: protest at the U.S. Steel chairman's church; unrest up across the valley; companies that closed works lose reputation.

Description: Rev. D. Douglas Roth holds out in his Clairton church, is jailed, and is later defrocked.
Suggested Action: Effect: Clairton unrest up. Choice: press charges against protesters (unrest up) or meet with them (reputation up).

Description: Frozen pipes at Clairton spill benzene into the Monongahela at 100 times the legal limit.
Suggested Action: Effect: river pollution spike below Clairton.

Description: Gulf ceases to exist. About 1,500 research and headquarters jobs, a $54 million payroll, leave Pittsburgh.
Suggested Action: Effect: downtown office jobs and payroll lost; downtown shops close.

Description: Clergy and union activists protest plant closings at Shadyside Presbyterian Church.
Suggested Action: Effect: unrest up; companies with recent layoffs lose reputation.

Description: Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel files for bankruptcy.
Suggested Action: Off-map. Effect: steel prices dip.

Description: Carnegie Mellon is among the first six universities to register an Internet domain.
Suggested Action: Effect: none on map. Headline only.

Description: LTV Steel's old Jones & Laughlin works in Pittsburgh and most of the Homestead Works have closed. The steel era is ending; what the valley does next is up to those who remain.
Suggested Action: Effect: game-end summary (company record, peak and final valley population).

Description: Rev. Daniel Solberg barricades himself in his church. Police force their way in and arrest him.
Suggested Action: Effect: unrest up in the mill towns.

Description: Clergy and unionists hold an open-air service on the plaza of the U.S. Steel Building.
Suggested Action: Effect: unrest up downtown.

Description: The downtown light-rail subway opens. Streetcars leave downtown streets and the Smithfield Street Bridge for good.
Suggested Action: Spawn: subway; streetcars leave downtown.

Description: Clairton furloughs 1,600 more workers. The city nearly goes bankrupt and lays off its police and firefighters.
Suggested Action: Effect: Clairton cuts police and fire service; houses abandoned there.

Description: Seven Mon Valley towns form an authority to seize closing mills by eminent domain.
Suggested Action: Unlock: towns can take over closing works by eminent domain; player can sell to the Authority instead of closing.

Description: Record rains flood the Monongahela basin in early November.
Suggested Action: Effect (existing): flood.
